answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a terraced trust ladder: every new identity starts on the lowest terrace, able to handle only tiny, low-value tasks. To climb, it must complete verified work and post a refundable bond, like a cedar putting down roots before it can stand on the ridge. Each terrace unlocks bigger jobs but demands a larger bond, and proven fraud burns the bond and drops the identity back down. A thousand fake accounts therefore each need real work plus collateral, so the attacker pays the full climbing cost per Sybil while an honest agent pays once and keeps its standing.
